beats.narration_en: Why do manhole covers sometimes blast into the air?
Under many streets, power cables run through underground vaults.
In winter, salty meltwater drips down onto old cables.
The salt eats at the insulation until electricity arcs.
The burning insulation gives off flammable gas that fills the vault.
One spark, and the gas explodes.
That can launch a cast iron cover weighing up to three hundred pounds.
So New York's utility is swapping in covers with vents.
Gas escapes through the holes instead of building up.
Others are latched: they pop up a few inches, vent, and drop back.
That's why some city manhole covers are full of holes.
